issueSummary: Water pipe leaking under washbasin in Science Complex B 3rd floor
studentProvidedFacts: Water pipe leaking under washbasin in Science Complex B 3rd floor
Small puddle forming near entrance door
visualObservations: Visible continuous drip from pipe P-trap coupling
aiInferences: High priority: Prevent water pooling from seeping into lower electrical risers

statusHistory.notes: Initial ticket generated and submitted via CampusFix AI.
Dispatched campus plumbing technician team with replacement PVC fittings.
Work verified and completed by senior campus technician.

notesThread.author: Marcus Vance (Facilities Lead)
notesThread.message: Plumbing crew on site at 09:30 AM; isolated isolation valve; replacing compromised rubber seal.

resolutionNotes: Replaced degraded P-trap compression gasket on sink #3. Pressure tested lines at 50 PSI for 15 minutes. No further leakage detected. Area sanitized and dried.

issueSummary: Intermittent Wi-Fi disconnects and low throughput on Campus-Secure around 2nd-floor quiet study pods
reportedLocation: Main University Library, 2nd Floor, East Wing Study Commons
imageObservations: Student attached screenshot of ping latency test showing 82% packet loss on 5GHz channel.
studentProvidedFacts: Affects multiple study desks in row E
aiInferences: Likely access point roaming failure or overloaded AP-LIB-2E unit
High student traffic area during midterm study weeks

statusHistory.notes: Submitted initial complaint with connectivity telemetry screenshot.
Dispatched network diagnostics team. Access point AP-LIB-2E power-cycled. Scheduled PoE switch replacement.

notesThread.author: David Kim (IT Network)
notesThread.message: Rebooted the local access point. We are observing improved ping times, but monitoring through peak library hours.

issueSummary: High-pressure water pipe leak under rinse basin pooling onto chemical storage floor
reportedLocation: Science Complex B, Room 104 Bio-Organic Chemistry Lab
imageObservations: Photo shows water spraying against cabinet wall under sink P-104 and pooling near electrical baseboard conduit.
studentProvidedFacts: Water spraying continuously under the secondary wash basin
Pool is spreading towards chemical cabinet 3
visualObservations: Ruptured PEX compression fitting visible near shutoff valve
Water pool approximately 3 inches from floor electrical junction box
aiInferences: Extreme safety hazard: high-pressure liquid near ground-level power conduit
Requires immediate emergency isolation valve shutdown

statusHistory.notes: Emergency shutoff valve isolated in hallway riser 4. Replacement brass valve kit ordered for installation.

notesThread.author: Robert Santos (Plumbing Dept)
notesThread.message: Water shutoff verified safe. Electrician inspected adjacent outlet and certified dry. Pipe replacement underway.

safetyWarning: Water accumulation within 1 meter of 120V electrical conduit. Power breaker isolated by facilities.

issueSummary: Rapidly flickering overhead fluorescent lighting tube emitting loud magnetic humming during lectures
imageObservations: Ceiling ballast panel shows dark discoloration on the right starter tube.
studentProvidedFacts: Back row lighting has been buzzing for two days
Tube strobes rapidly when turned to maximum brightness
visualObservations: Visible phosphor burn-in on ends of T8 fluorescent tube
aiInferences: Ballast capacitor failure or degraded tube filament
No immediate fire hazard, but high lecture distraction

statusHistory.notes: Ticket queued for routine electrical maintenance inspection.

issueSummary: Spilled coffee and shattered ceramic mug on main pedestrian marble corridor
reportedLocation: Student Activity Center, Level 1 Main Concourse by South Entry
imageObservations: Brown beverage puddle approximately 4 feet wide with ceramic fragments on slick floor tile.
studentProvidedFacts: Someone dropped a full mug and walked away
Multiple students nearly slipped walking toward the turnstiles
visualObservations: Liquid pool with sharp ceramic shards on polished terrazzo flooring
aiInferences: Immediate slip-and-fall liability in heavy foot-traffic threshold

statusHistory.notes: Safety cones positioned. Mobile wet-vac dispatch.
Corridor thoroughly swept for glass shards, mop-sanitized with degreaser, and floor blower dried.

resolutionNotes: Glass swept with magnetic broom, entire concourse section scrubbed, disinfected, and air-dried. Wet floor signs cleared after final supervisor sign-off.

notesThread.author: Maria Alvarez (Sanitation)
notesThread.message: All ceramic remnants removed. Floor dried and inspected.
